summary: advisory target version is recorded without the v prefix
detail: plan for the spike module proposed golang.org/x/sys 0.44.0 while go.mod records v0.41.0; go get accepts either but the plan is internally inconsistent.
hint: Normalize fixed versions from OSV into the ecosystem's spelling when the plan is built, so a target reads v0.44.0 like every other Go version in the plan.

detail: RunOnce always stops before publishing, with the summary text saying so, even when auto_pr is true.
hint: Honour defaults.auto_pr in RunOnce: when true and verification passed, call OpenPullRequest for each group instead of stopping at the branch.

summary: no panic recovery at MCP tool boundaries
detail: wrap() records unexpected errors but a panic never reaches it.
hint: Wrap tool handlers with a defer/recover that records a KindInternal fault and returns an isError result, so a panic is journaled instead of vanishing into the transport.

summary: yarn berry is refused rather than supported
detail: v2eco detects a berry yarn.lock and Inventory returns an error.
hint: Implement a berry lockfile reader (__metadata, checksum, PnP) as a separate ecosystem; the v1 reader deliberately rejects it.

summary: OSV fixed versions without a v prefix were dropped by policy
a plan depmcp built itself is rejected as PLAN_STALE because the duplicate-change check ignores the target
detail: apply_plan on rMath (plan 4bd35c50a3eaa7aa): PLAN_STALE 'plan is not self-consistent: [duplicate change for actions/checkout@v7.0.1]'. The plan held actions/checkout v4 -> v7.0.1 twice because ci.yml and lean.yml both pin it and the scan reported one dependency per workflow file, all under the single target actions:/.github/workflows.
hint: Identify a change by the file it edits as well as the dependency, and report one dependency per (target, name) so a target owning several manifests does not turn one action into two changes.

summary: plan_updates panics when the plan has no groups
detail: depmcp plan on a git repository with no manifests: panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 at internal/app/readpath.go:513 (SavePlan with plan.Groups[0].Target). The MCP boundary turns this into INTERNAL_ERROR, so a repository whose dependencies are all current cannot be planned at all.
hint: Record an empty plan with an empty target row instead of indexing the first group; firstTarget already exists for this on the write path.

summary: the actions applier rewrites any ref, so a plan built from the working tree can be applied to a different base and the commit states the wrong from-version
detail: Verification of the PLAN_STALE fix: the plan was built from a working tree where both workflows pinned actions/checkout@v4, while the clone's default branch still had @v7. Apply based the run on the default branch, the applier matched the action by name and rewrote the v7 lines to the v7.0.1 SHA, and the commit message read 'actions/checkout v4 -> v7.0.1 (major)' with Observed reporting v7 as the from-version. The rewritten file is a correct hardened pin, but the record of it is wrong.
hint: Either make the actions applier honour Change.From and report the lines it actually changed, or build the plan from the same fetched default branch apply will use, so Observed and the commit message describe the diff that was really produced.

summary: apply ignores a group's target, so a plan for a sub-module manifest is applied to the repository root
detail: applyGroups calls ecosystem.Apply(ctx, run.Worktree, changes) for every group, so dir is always the repository root while gomod.Apply reads filepath.Join(dir, go.mod). A plan built from a monorepo with go.mod in the root and in svc/ therefore runs go get for both groups against the root go.mod: the sub-module change either lands in the wrong file or, now that appliers verify the from-ref, is refused as PLAN_STALE. The same blindness affects docker (a plan for web/Dockerfile) and maven (any second pom). Found while fixing DEP-D516B032; the plan side now allows two targets to share a dependency and version, which makes this reachable more often.
hint: Give the applier the target it is working on: either pass the target's directory as dir (with an ecosystem-level rule for ecosystems whose Apply already means the whole repository, such as the workflows directory) or add ApplyIn(ctx, root, target, changes) to the interface.

summary: the delegated appliers record the requested change as the observation
detail: v2eco Python's delegated path (pip/uv/poetry), and Cargo/Yarn/Berry, set res.Observed[ch.Name] = {ch.From, ch.To} straight from the change instead of reading the lockfile back. gomod and nodejs do read back. Consequence: a toolchain that resolved something other than what was asked is invisible in the run record, and the apply-boundary check added for DEP-D516B032 cannot catch a version disagreement for those ecosystems, because the observation always matches the plan by construction.
hint: Read the manifest or lockfile back after the toolchain runs, the way nodejs and gomod already do, so Observed is a measurement rather than an echo of the request.

summary: the plan is built from the working tree while apply bases on the default branch
detail: On rMath: plan_updates reads the files on disk and proposes actions/checkout v7 -> v7.0.1, setup-python v7 -> v7.1.0, because the checked-out branch chore/codewitness-depmcp-pass (2c20151) pins the current majors. apply_plan creates its worktree from the repository's default branch, origin/main (4fbc2e8), which still pins v4/v5, so the run now fails with PLAN_STALE: 'actions/checkout is v4, the plan expects v7; actions/setup-python is v5, the plan expects v7 (…, based on origin/main)'. Before the from-ref check this applied silently and committed a diff described as v7 -> v7.0.1. Either way, a user on a branch ahead of the default branch cannot update it through depmcp.
hint: Build the plan from the same ref apply will use — a temporary worktree, or the manifests read with git show <ref>:<path> — or record the base ref in the plan and refuse at plan time when the working tree differs from it.
